q: Singles. The receiver is in a wheelchair. An otherwise correct service bounces on the receiver's court, then spins back towards the net. The receiver can't reach it. What is your decision?

diagram.alt: Side view: after bouncing on the receiver's court the ball spins back towards the net

detail: When the receiver is in a wheelchair due to a physical disability, the rally is a **let** if an otherwise correct service, **after touching the receiver's court, returns in the direction of the net**. The same applies if it comes to rest on the receiver's court or, in singles, leaves it by either side line.

q: How are Para table tennis sport classes grouped?
detail: Players are classified as **classes 1–5 for wheelchair players**, **6–10 for standing players** and **class 11 for players with an intellectual disability**.

q: Within the Para classes, what does a lower class number mean?
detail: **The lower the number of the class, the more severe the disability.** The player's International Classification Card (ICC) records the class and any limitations, for example on making a legal service.

q: A player in a wheelchair wants to wear tracksuit trousers during play. Do they need the referee's permission?
options: No: players with a physical disability may wear tracksuit trousers, but not jeans
No, and jeans are also allowed
detail: A player with a physical disability, in a wheelchair or standing, **may wear the trousers portion of a tracksuit during play without the referee's permission**, but **jeans are not permitted**.

q: Singles. The receiver is in a wheelchair. An otherwise correct service bounces on the receiver's court, then leaves it over a side line. The receiver doesn't touch it. What is your decision?

diagram.alt: Top view: after bouncing on the receiver's court the service goes out over the side line

detail: In singles, when the receiver is in a wheelchair, it is a **let** if an otherwise correct service, after touching the receiver's court, **leaves it by either side line**. The ball may cross the side line after one or more bounces.

q: Singles, receiver in a wheelchair. A service is heading for the side line, but the receiver strikes it before it crosses the line. Is it a let?
options: No: the service is good and play continues
Yes: it was going over the side line
detail: If the ball is travelling towards the side line but **the receiver strikes it before it crosses the side line** (or takes a second bounce), **the service is considered good and no let is called**.

q: DOUBLES, the receiver is in a wheelchair, and the service is otherwise correct. Which of these make the rally a let? Select all that apply.
options: The ball comes to rest on the receiver's court
After bouncing, the ball returns towards the net
The ball touches the net, then lands in the correct half-court
The ball leaves the receiver's court over a side line
detail: Coming to rest and **returning towards the net** are lets in singles and doubles. The **side line** rule applies **in singles only**. A net service landing correctly is a let for everyone.

q: Both players are in wheelchairs. Reaching for a ball, a player lifts both thighs off the seat just before striking it. What is your decision?
options: Play on: it is allowed if the return is good
detail: When both players are in wheelchairs, a player must keep **minimum contact with the seat or cushion with the back of at least one thigh** when striking the ball. Losing that contact gives the opponent the point.

q: Both players are in wheelchairs. A player leans on the table with the free hand for support, then strikes the ball. What is your decision?
options: Play on, if the table did not move
detail: When both players are in wheelchairs, the opponent scores if a player **touches the table with either hand before striking the ball**. The free hand may never be used on the table as support, and must not touch the playing surface during the rally.

q: Both players are in wheelchairs. When may a player touch the table?
options: Only with the racket hand, after playing a shot, to restore balance, provided the playing surface does not move
With either hand at any time
With the free hand to restore balance after a shot
detail: A player may touch the table **only with the racket hand, to restore balance, only after a shot has been played**, provided **the playing surface does not move**. In doubles only the player who struck the ball may do this.

q: Both players are in wheelchairs. During play, a player's footrest touches the floor. What is your decision?
detail: When both players or pairs are in wheelchairs, the opponent scores if a player's **footrest or foot touches the floor during play**.

q: Doubles, where at least one player of a pair is in a wheelchair. What is the order of play?
options: Server serves, receiver returns, then either player of that pair may return
The normal alternating doubles order throughout
The wheelchair player must play every return
Either player may serve or receive
detail: The **server makes a service, the receiver makes a return**, but **thereafter either player of the pair with a wheelchair player may make returns**.

q: Doubles. A pair has one wheelchair player and one standing player. During a rally, the standing player's foot crosses the imaginary extension of the centre line. What is your decision?
options: Play on: only wheelchairs are restricted
detail: Where an opposing pair includes at least one wheelchair player, a point is awarded if **any part of the wheelchair or a foot of a standing player crosses the imaginary extension of the centre line**. Each player must stay in their own half.

umpire.signal: Point signal towards the opposing pair

q: What is the maximum total height of a wheelchair player's cushion (one or two cushions)?
detail: The height of one, or at most two, cushions is limited to **15 cm**, with no other addition to the wheelchair. The wheelchair must also have **at least two large wheels and one small wheel** throughout a rally.

q: A Para player is temporarily unable to play because of their condition. What may the referee allow?
options: After consulting a medical classifier or doctor, medical recovery time as short as possible, at most 10 minutes
Nothing: the match is awarded to the opponent
detail: The referee may, **after consulting a medical classifier or doctor**, allow **medical recovery time** of the shortest practical duration, and **in no circumstances more than 10 minutes**.

q: For a match with wheelchair players, what should the umpire also check before play? Select all that apply.
options: The number of wheels on the wheelchair
That no backpack hangs on the back of the wheelchair
Name and 3-letter Association code on the back of the shirt
detail: Pre-match checks for wheelchair play: **number of wheels**, **no backpack** on the chair, **cushion height**, **tracksuit trousers and no jeans**, and **name and 3-letter Association code** on the back of the shirt.
